# Sample Size for Sensitivity and Specificity {#sec-sensitivity-specificity}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Identify separate diseased and non-diseased requirements.
- Convert stratum targets to an expected recruitment total.
:::

## The idea

Sensitivity is the proportion of reference-standard-positive participants testing positive; specificity is the proportion of reference-standard-negative participants testing negative. Their precision depends on **different denominators**. A study that estimates both must plan adequate numbers of participants with and without the target condition. Expected disease prevalence becomes important when recruiting from one undifferentiated clinical population.

## When and how to apply it

A simple Wald approximation for sensitivity precision is $n_D\approx Z^2 Se(1-Se)/d^2$, where $n_D$ is the number of diseased participants. The current calculator also offers Wilson-based anticipated intervals. Separate target quotas and an expected prevalence-based total should not be conflated with guaranteed counts.

## Formula at a glance

$$
n_D\approx\frac{Z^2Se(1-Se)}{d^2}\qquad n_{ND}\approx\frac{Z^2Sp(1-Sp)}{d^2}
$$


## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
For anticipated sensitivity 0.85 and half-width 0.05 at 95% confidence, the Wald expression gives $1.96^2(0.85)(0.15)/(0.05^2)=195.92$, or **196 diseased participants**. Additional non-diseased participants are needed to estimate specificity.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Calculation logic

The example uses the stated planning assumptions and mathematical approximation. Explain why they apply before reporting the numerical result.

### Copy-and-run R

```r
z <- qnorm(.975); se <- .85; d <- .05
ceiling(z^2 * se * (1-se) / d^2)
```

:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
A required 196 diseased participants does not mean that recruiting 196 unselected clinic attendees will suffice.
:::

Repeat for anticipated specificity 0.90; combine the two stratum targets under expected prevalence 20%, and state the limitations of expected recruitment.
